title: Explicit pullback scalar cone comparison in normalized word coordinates
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure, allowing equality, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_F$, uniformizers $\varpi_F$, and $A_{F,n}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ for $F=E,L$ and $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism, with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site of $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], set $B_{F,W,n}=(A_{F,n})_W$ and $R_{F,W}=\lim_n B_{F,W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ambient derived categories of these completed-ring module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ be constructible and derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $\widehat U_{g,F}=Lg_F^*$ for completed integral pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] and $\widehat S_W=T_{L/E,W}$ for completed integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension].

Let $\mathscr S_F(W)$ be the category of strict quotient-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, $\mathcal R_{F,W}$ its simultaneous derived reduction functor, $\mathcal L_{F,W}=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ its realization functor, and $e:\mathcal R\mathcal L\to1$ the entire-system counit [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A system is normalized if its transition-adjoint maps $C_m\otimes^L_{B_{F,W,m}}B_{F,W,n}\to C_n$ are isomorphisms for $m\geq n$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Use the whole-system operations $U_{g,F}$ and $S_W=S_{L/E,W}$ and their specified scalar/pullback comparison $\kappa:S_XU_{g,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{g,L}S_Y$ [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Put
$$C=\mathcal R_{E,Y}K,\qquad A=S_XU_{g,E}C,\qquad B=U_{g,L}S_YC.$$

Supply any simultaneous primitive realization models with the normalization of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]: actual quotient transitions, balanced scalar association, quotient augmentation with zero shifted Roos coordinate, and the ordinary-limit-cone counit on K-injective tower resolutions. Assume $C,U_{g,E}C,S_YC,A,B$ are normalized with constructible-complete intermediate realizations and invertible counits. For primitive operations $O$, write $b_{O,H}:\widehat OH\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal LO\mathcal RH$ for the prescribed normalized realization isomorphisms and put
$$r_{O,D}=\mathcal L(O(e_D))\circ b_{O,\mathcal LD}.$$
Define the two word coordinates by
$$\beta_A=r_{S_X,U_{g,E}C}\circ\widehat S_X(b_{U_{g,E},K}),\qquad
\beta_B=r_{U_{g,L},S_YC}\circ\widehat U_{g,L}(b_{S_Y,K}).$$
Thus $\beta_A:\widehat S_X\widehat U_{g,E}K\to\mathcal L_{L,X}A$ and $\beta_B:\widehat U_{g,L}\widehat S_YK\to\mathcal L_{L,X}B$.

For a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], put $Q=P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}R_{L,Y}$. Use the specified comparison $\alpha_K$, tower maps $d_n$, cone map $\delta_P$ and completion maps $\chi$ of [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha]. Explicitly, for $M$ an $R_{F,Y}$-complex put
$$D^F_n(M)=\operatorname{Res}^F_n g^*(M\otimes_{R_{F,Y}}B_{F,Y,n}),\quad
A_F(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nD^F_n(M)\to\prod_nD^F_n(M))[-1],$$
where $s$ uses the actual quotient transitions and $g^*$ is module inverse image along the coefficient structure maps. With $\iota_n:A_{E,n}\to A_{L,n}$ induced by the coefficient inclusion and $\pi^L_n:R_{L,X}\to B_{L,X,n}$ the projection, the map $d_n:D^E_n(P)\otimes_{R_{E,X}}R_{L,X}\to D^L_n(Q)$ is
$$((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes t\longmapsto(g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_n(\bar a)))\otimes\bigl(\iota_n(b)\pi^L_n(t)\bigr).$$
Here $p,\bar a,b,t$ are local tensor generators over $R_{E,Y},B_{E,Y,n},B_{E,X,n},R_{L,X}$ respectively; tensors mean sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and inverse image uses [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Under the canonical tensor/product comparisons, $\delta_P:A_E(P)\otimes_{R_{E,X}}R_{L,X}\to A_L(Q)$ applies $\prod_n d_n$ to both Roos cone coordinates. The maps $\chi$ are the quotient augmentations with zero shifted coordinate, and
$$\alpha_K=\widehat U_{g,L}(\chi_{Y,K})\circ[\delta_P]\circ\chi_{X,\widehat U_{g,E}K}^{-1}.$$

In these prescribed word coordinates, the derived-system localization $\kappa^D:S_XU_{g,E}C\to U_{g,L}S_YC$ of balanced scalar association is exactly $\kappa_C$. On these same simultaneous quotient presentations its realized tensor map is the displayed $d_n$ on both cone coordinates, with the stated augmentation normalization. Consequently the specified tensor-and-completion arrow has the normalization
$$\beta_B\circ\alpha_K=\mathcal L_{L,X}(\kappa_C)\circ\beta_A.$$
These are identities of the specified derived morphisms, natural in $K$ and independent of $P$ through canonical resolution comparisons. No flatness of the finite quotient-ring maps and no finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Choose a simultaneous normalized comparison system D using ambientComparisonSystem_exists. The normalized Roos models supplied in the statement equal those of D: resolve any tower complex into a K-injective tower, use the computes equations to identify the two comparisons there, and cancel the image of the resolution using naturality. This is equality of whole natural Roos comparisons.

Apply PrimitiveReductionTransport.realizations_transport to the supplied and simultaneous reduction calculi. This independently proved helper transports quotient presentations, their whole-system unit/augmentation coherence and the normalized primitive realizations through the canonical leftAdjointUniq comparison. Its two conclusions give b_S ; L(O(a)) = b_T for pullback and scalar extension, respectively.

The two word coordinates respect this transport, including their actual intermediate counits. First use naturality of b to rewrite H(f);b;L(O(e)) as b;L(O(R(f);e)). Naturality of the actual counit moves an initial-system transport a0 past e, replacing f by f;L(a0). Naturality of the intermediate left-adjoint comparison a1 and leftAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit identify R(f);e with a1;Rprime(f);eprime. The primitive equality of the preceding step cancels a1. Apply this categorical calculation to the source word and the target word, obtaining betaA_supplied ; L(S_X U_E a0) = betaA_D and betaB_supplied ; L(U_L S_Y a0) = betaB_D.

In system D, expand the whole-system pullback and scalar counits and use naturality of the primitive realizations to identify betaA_D with lambda and betaB_D with mu followed by L(kappa). integralScalarPullbackCompletion_normalization gives alpha ; mu = lambda for precisely scalarPullbackCompleted, with the completeness proof supplied by specifiedPullbackComparisonAlpha. Therefore alpha ; betaB_D = betaA_D ; L(kappa).

Postcompose the required supplied-model equality with L(U_L S_Y a0), which is invertible. Substitute both transported-word identities. The D-model square from the preceding step and naturality of the whole-system kappa at a0 identify the results. Cancel the isomorphism. This is equality of complete derived-system morphisms, without any faithfulness assertion about individual finite evaluations.

Supplemental whole-system localization clause: apply the normalization property of integralComparisonSystemScalarPullback obtained from its existence-and-uniqueness theorem to the supplied K-flat strict quotient system. This identifies the two entire derived system arrows, not merely their finite evaluations.

proof.text: Supplemental finite-level generator clause: conjugate the strict-cone data level map by the canonical generator-normalized isomorphism from integralOrdinaryScalar to completedOrdinaryScalarExtension, on both schemes. Naturality of the coefficient pullback adjunction unit and of unrestricted reduction proves that scalarPullbackGenerator commutes with chain maps. At unit generators the conjugated map satisfies scalarPullbackLevelNormalization, so uniqueness identifies it with scalarPullbackLevel. The full strict-data generator formula then gives the displayed arbitrary a,b,s formula. The inverse scalar-model isomorphism sends the completed tensor section to its ordinary counterpart by the inverse identity.
